channel.title: The ArmChair Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The ArmChair Journal (armchairjournal.com)

item.title: After India: Is Pakistan facing a 2.5-front war?
item.description: New tensions across South Asia are reshaping Pakistan's security outlook - with issues about Durand Line, Kashmir and Internal Security.

item.title: Dhaka and Islamabad: South Asia’s politics in transition
item.description: Bangladesh has been facing a political unrest after Sheikh Hasina fled the country. Imran Khan's arrest in Pakistan also raises questions concerning power and justice.

item.title: Short Story: One Never Returns to Hiraeth
item.description: A story of how change in a village, Hiraeth, is discussed between Gul and her father when they visit Hiraeth for a local festival, Chitrani.

item.title: Caste Census and OBC backwardness: The Tamil Nadu Model
item.description: Tamil Nadu model suggests fair representation to OBCs can ensure social justice without compromising economic growth

item.title: Free-riders of Freedom: Political parties
item.description: Cash transfers are on the rise in India, compromising capital expenditures. Using game theory, political parties can be modelled in an externalities problem.

item.title: Sino-Taiwan tensions and India’s strategic dilemma
item.description: Developing tensions in the Taiwan strait have consequences for India and the world as one-fifth of global maritime trade goes through the strait, unlike the crowded Malacca strait. Amidst One China Policy and unofficial relations with Taiwan, India must ensure its tech supply chains are secured.

item.title: Coaching Classrooms, Or what do you call a group of parrots?
item.description: Under the lure of a good life, coaching centres in India exploit the dreams of parents and put students into cages that can't dream

item.title: Learning in an Unfamiliar Tongue? Reflections from a Delhi School
item.description: Most Indian schools have children who have different mother-tongues compared to medium of instruction. This poses unique learning challenges to policymakers.

item.title: Great power rush in melting Arctic: Where does India stand?
item.description: Melting ice in the arctic and possibilities of energy resources has led to the US, Russia and China recalibrating their arctic positing. India must play a role too.

item.title: Western democracies on the edge? Polarisation, protests, and the battle for legitimacy
item.description: Western democracies have been seeing a crisis of legitimacy as citizens are not trusting institutions and governments anymore. What would this lead to?
